Accra de Morue with Pikliz

Served at: Fete de Papa Zaka - Feast of the Farmer Loa

Serves 4-6Prep 45 min (plus overnight soaking for cod)Cook 25 min

Accra de Morue are savory, crispy salt cod fritters, a beloved staple in Haitian cuisine. Paired with Pikliz, a vibrant and spicy pickled vegetable relish, this dish offers a delightful contrast of textures and flavors. It represents the hearty, flavorful, and often humble fare offered during Fete de Papa Zaka, honoring the spirit of agriculture and the bounty of the land that Papa Zaka, the farmer Loa, protects.

Ingredients

  • For the Accra de Morue:
  • 1 lb (450g) salt cod
  • 1 1/2 cups (180g) all-purpose flour
  • 1 tsp baking powder
  • 1/2 tsp black pepper
  • 2 large eggs
  • 1/2 cup (120ml) water, or as needed
  • 1/2 medium yellow onion, finely chopped
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1/2 Scotch bonnet pepper, seeded and minced (or to taste)
  • 2 scallions, thinly sliced
  • 2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped
  • 1 tsp fresh thyme leaves
  • Vegetable oil, for deep frying
  • For the Pikliz:
  • 1/2 small head green cabbage, thinly shredded (about 3 cups)
  • 2 medium carrots, julienned or shredded
  • 1 bell pepper (any color), thinly sliced
  • 1/2 small red onion, thinly sliced
  • 1-2 Scotch bonnet peppers, left whole or sliced (for more heat)
  • 1 cup (240ml) white vinegar
  • 2 tbsp (30ml) fresh lime juice
  • 1 tsp salt
  • 1/2 tsp black peppercorns (optional)
  • 2-3 whole cloves (optional)

Method

  1. For the Accra de Morue: Begin by desalting the salt cod. Rinse the cod thoroughly under cold water. Place it in a large bowl, cover with fresh cold water, and soak for at least 12-24 hours, changing the water 3-4 times. After soaking, drain the cod, place it in a pot with fresh water, bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10-15 minutes until tender. Drain, let cool slightly, then flake the cod, removing any skin or bones.
  2. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, and black pepper.
  3. In a separate bowl, whisk the eggs and water until combined.
  4. Add the flaked cod, chopped onion, minced garlic, minced Scotch bonnet pepper, sliced scallions, chopped parsley, and thyme leaves to the dry ingredients. Mix well.
  5. Gradually add the egg mixture to the cod and flour mixture, stirring until just combined. The batter should be thick but spoonable; add a little more water if it's too stiff.
  6. Heat about 2-3 inches (5-7.5 cm) of vegetable oil in a deep pot or Dutch oven to 350°F (175°C).
  7. Carefully drop spoonfuls of the batter into the hot oil, being careful not to overcrowd the pot. Fry for 3-5 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through.
  8. Remove the accra with a slotted spoon and place them on a plate lined with paper towels to drain excess oil. Keep warm while frying the remaining batches.
  9. For the Pikliz: In a large glass jar or bowl, combine the shredded cabbage, julienned carrots, sliced bell pepper, and sliced red onion. Add the whole or sliced Scotch bonnet peppers.
  10. In a separate small bowl, whisk together the white vinegar, lime juice, and salt. If using, add the black peppercorns and whole cloves to the vinegar mixture.
  11. Pour the vinegar mixture over the vegetables in the jar. Press down on the vegetables to ensure they are mostly submerged in the liquid. If needed, add a little more vinegar to cover.
  12. Cover the jar tightly and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or preferably overnight, to allow the flavors to meld. The Pikliz will keep well in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks.
  13. Serve the warm Accra de Morue immediately with a generous side of Pikliz.

Tips

  • For less heat in the Pikliz, use fewer Scotch bonnet peppers or remove the seeds and membranes before adding them.
  • Ensure your oil is at the correct temperature for frying; too cool and the accra will be greasy, too hot and they will burn on the outside before cooking through.
  • You can prepare the Pikliz a day or two in advance to allow the flavors to fully develop, making it even more vibrant.
